channel.title: Farmer's Weekly SA - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Farmer's Weekly SA (farmersweekly.co.za)

item.title: Commercial beekeeping: managing swarms and logistics
item.description: Managing thousands of bee colonies as a pollination service provider is a complex, logistical feat. Added to the challenge is keeping the swarms fed amid dwindling natural resources and crops that offer little nutrition. Jaco Wolfaardt, commercial beekeeper and founder of Ubusi Beekeeping, spoke to Henning Naudé about keeping the bees and business abuzz.

item.title: Managing ascites in broilers starts with prevention
item.description: Ascites is one of the most economically damaging conditions in broiler production. It often becomes visible late in the production cycle but starts much earlier, and once clinical signs appear, there is no treatment, thus producers must remain vigilant.

item.title: Experts step in to guide farmers through FMD crisis
item.description: As South Africa’s foot-and-mouth disease outbreak escalates into what experts are calling an unprecedented livestock crisis, scientists, veterinarians, and agriculture specialists have formally stepped in to give farmers practical, science-based guidance while the country awaits the vaccine rollout.

item.title: Fast-growing free-range Pekin ducks offer niche market opportunities
item.description: Vanessa Collocott runs a free-range Pekin duck enterprise in Curry’s Post, KwaZulu-Natal. She explains that with a seven-week production cycle, disciplined management, and secure restaurant markets, duck farming provides steady cash flow and a viable diversification option for small-scale farmers.

item.title: Drop in fuel prices brings welcome relief to farmers
item.description: The latest official fuel price adjustments published by the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources (DMPR) show that petrol prices have fallen by around 65c/ℓ, while diesel prices have declined by between 50c and 57c/ℓ, depending on grade.

item.title: Farmers fear reforms may come too late as wheat crisis deepens
item.description: Grain SA and Minister of Agriculture John Steenhuisen are pushing for urgent reforms to support wheat farmers, but many producers are concerned that it may be too little, too late.

item.title: Steenhuisen’s ministerial future could hinge on new DA leader
item.description: Minister of Agriculture John Steenhuisen has announced that he will not seek re-election as DA leader, but he will remain in his ministerial post, adding that he now intends to focus all his energy on combating the country’s devastating foot-and-mouth disease outbreak.

item.title: Mark Hook leads revival of Boran, Nkone cattle societies in Zimbabwe
item.description: Zimbabwean farmer Mark Hook has revived dormant Boran and Nkone cattle societies, growing registered herds from a handful to thousands. He spoke to Farmer’s Weekly about his role in reshaping the country’s cattle industry.

item.title: FMD vaccine urgency grows amid state procurement contradictions
item.description: South Africa’s worsening foot-and-mouth disease crisis highlights the urgent need to rapidly secure and distribute as many effective vaccines as possible to protect the national herd and stabilise an industry already under severe strain.

item.title: Optimal swine nutrition: don’t feed more, but feed better
item.description: A one-size-fits-all diet for pigs can lead to overfeeding or underfeeding, producing varying results, and lost production. Instead, JD Mostert, independent swine nutritionist, advocates for a stronger focus on digestible amino acids to get the most from feed rations.
